meta.description: Allow authorised users to manually add a new credit card transaction record to the CardDemo transaction ledger.
meta.process_description: The program presents a data-entry screen where a bank operator can record a new credit card transaction by supplying either an Account ID or a Card Number (the system cross-references the other automatically), together with full transaction details such as type, category, source, amount, description, origination date, processing date, and merchant information. All entered fields are validated for completeness, correct format, and referential integrity (account/card must exist in the cross-reference file) before the transaction is written. The operator must explicitly confirm the addition (Y/N prompt) before the record is committed to the TRANSACT file, providing a deliberate two-step authorisation safeguard against accidental data entry.

files.TRANSACT: Master transaction ledger where new credit card transaction records are permanently stored
files.ACCTDAT: Account master file used to validate that the referenced account exists and retrieve account details
files.CCXREF: Card-to-account cross-reference file used to look up the Account ID associated with a given Card Number
files.CXACAIX: Alternate index on the cross-reference file used to look up the Card Number associated with a given Account ID

business_rules: Either an Account ID or a Card Number must be provided; the system will automatically resolve and populate the other via the cross-reference file — both cannot be blank.
Account ID must be numeric and must exist in the card-to-account cross-reference (CXACAIX); an invalid or non-existent account is rejected.
Card Number must be numeric and must exist in the card-to-account cross-reference (CCXREF); an invalid or non-existent card number is rejected.

All transaction fields are mandatory: Transaction Type Code, Category Code, Source, Description, Amount, Origination Date, Processing Date, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, and Merchant Zip.
Transaction Type Code and Category Code must be numeric values.
Transaction dates (Origination Date and Processing Date) must be valid calendar dates, verified by calling the CSUTLDTC date-validation utility.

The operator must explicitly confirm the transaction addition by entering 'Y' in the confirmation field; entering 'N' or leaving it blank re-displays the screen with a prompt to confirm, preventing accidental writes.
If the session is entered without a prior communication area (EIBCALEN = 0), the user is redirected to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C), enforcing authenticated access.

PF3 returns the operator to the calling program (or the main menu COMEN01C if no calling program is recorded), PF4 clears the current screen, and PF5 copies the last transaction's data onto the form to assist with repetitive data entry.

This paragraph creates and permanently records a new credit card transaction in the master transaction ledger. It assigns the next available unique transaction ID, populates the full transaction record from the operator's screen input, and writes it to the ledger.
Sets the search key to the highest possible value so the file browse will position at the very end of the transaction ledger, enabling retrieval of the last-used transaction ID.
Opens a backward browse on the transaction ledger, starting from the end of the file, to locate the most recently assigned transaction ID.
Reads the last transaction record in the ledger to retrieve the highest existing transaction ID currently in use.
Closes the backward browse on the transaction ledger now that the last transaction ID has been retrieved.
Captures the most recently used transaction ID as a numeric value so arithmetic can be performed on it.
Increments the last-used transaction ID by one to generate the next unique transaction identifier for the new record.
Clears the transaction record buffer to ensure no residual data from a previous operation contaminates the new transaction being built.
Stamps the newly generated unique transaction ID onto the new transaction record.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Top-level working storage group holding all general-purpose operational variables used throughout the transaction add process.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal name of this program (COTRN02C), used when transferring control to other screens or recording which program initiated an action — ensures the system knows where to return after a sub-task completes.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier (CT02) assigned to the Add Transaction function. Used when invoking this screen via CICS so the system routes the operator to the correct program.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: The status or error message displayed at the bottom of the screen to guide the operator — for example, confirming a transaction was added successfully, or explaining why a submission was rejected (e.g., invalid account, missing field).

variables.name: WS-TRANSACT-FILE
variables.description: The logical file name of the master transaction ledger (TRANSACT) where new credit card transaction records are permanently written once the operator confirms the addition.

variables.name: WS-ACCTDAT-FILE
variables.description: The logical file name of the account master file (ACCTDAT) used to verify that the account referenced in the new transaction actually exists and is on record.

variables.name: WS-CCXREF-FILE
variables.description: The logical file name of the card-to-account cross-reference file (CCXREF), used to look up the Account ID associated with a given Card Number entered by the operator.

variables.name: WS-CXACAIX-FILE
variables.description: The logical file name of the alternate index on the cross-reference file (CXACAIX), used to look up the Card Number associated with a given Account ID when the operator provides an account number instead of a card number.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: Error flag that controls whether the transaction add screen is re-displayed with a validation error rather than proceeding to write the record. Set to 'Y' whenever a business rule violation is detected (e.g., missing field, invalid account), preventing the transaction from being saved until all errors are corrected.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: Condition name indicating that at least one validation error has been found on the transaction entry form. When true, the screen is re-displayed with an appropriate error message instead of saving the transaction.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that no validation errors have been detected on the transaction entry form. When true, processing can continue toward saving the transaction record.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after each file I/O or service call (e.g., reading the account file or writing the transaction). A non-zero value signals that the operation failed, triggering error handling to protect data integrity.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code that provides additional detail about why a file or service operation failed. Used alongside WS-RESP-CD to diagnose specific problems such as a record not found or a file being unavailable.

variables.name: WS-USR-MODIFIED
variables.description: Flag that tracks whether the operator has changed any field on the transaction entry screen since it was last displayed. Used to determine whether re-validation is needed before attempting to save the transaction.

variables.name: USR-MODIFIED-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating the operator has actively changed one or more fields on the transaction form, requiring the system to re-validate all inputs before proceeding.

variables.name: USR-MODIFIED-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating the operator has not changed any fields since the screen was last shown, meaning previously validated data can be trusted without re-validation.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-AMT
variables.description: Formatted display buffer for the transaction amount, including sign, used for intermediate formatting during screen I/O. Supports amounts up to $99,999,999.99 with an explicit positive or negative sign to represent credits and debits.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-DATE
variables.description: The transaction date being validated or processed during the add transaction workflow. Holds the date value prior to format validation by the CSUTLDTC utility to confirm it is a real calendar date.

variables.name: WS-ACCT-ID-N
variables.description: Numeric form of the Account ID entered by the operator or resolved automatically via the card-to-account cross-reference lookup. Used for file key comparisons and validation against the account master file to confirm the account exists.

variables.name: WS-CARD-NUM-N
variables.description: Numeric form of the 16-digit Card Number entered by the operator or resolved automatically via the account-to-card cross-reference lookup. Used as the file key when reading the CCXREF cross-reference file to validate the card and retrieve its linked account.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-ID-N
variables.description: Numeric form of the unique Transaction ID assigned to the new transaction record being added. Used internally to construct or reference the transaction key when writing to the master transaction ledger.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-AMT-N
variables.description: Signed numeric transaction amount used for internal calculation and storage. Holds the exact monetary value (up to $999,999,999.99, positive for charges and negative for credits) that will be written into the transaction ledger record.

variables.name: WS-TRAN-AMT-E
variables.description: Formatted display version of the transaction amount shown on the operator's screen. Presents the amount with an explicit sign and decimal point so the operator can clearly see whether the transaction is a charge or a credit before confirming.

variables.name: WS-DATE-FORMAT
variables.description: The expected date format string (YYYY-MM-DD) passed to the CSUTLDTC date-validation utility when checking the Origination Date and Processing Date entered by the operator. Ensures all dates conform to the system's standard format before the transaction is accepted.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-PARM
variables.description: Parameter block passed to the CSUTLDTC date-validation utility. Contains the date to be checked, the expected format, and fields to receive the validation result — used to confirm that Origination and Processing Dates entered by the operator are genuine calendar dates.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-DATE
variables.description: The specific date value (e.g., the Origination Date or Processing Date from the transaction form) passed to the CSUTLDTC utility for calendar validation. If this date is not a real date, the transaction is rejected.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-DATE-FORMAT
variables.description: The date format string (populated from WS-DATE-FORMAT, i.e., YYYY-MM-DD) sent to the CSUTLDTC utility so it knows how to interpret the date being validated. Ensures consistent date parsing across all transaction date fields.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-RESULT
variables.description: Group field containing the outcome of the date validation call to CSUTLDTC. The program inspects these fields to determine whether the date entered by the operator is valid and, if not, what error message to display.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-RESULT-SEV-CD
variables.description: Severity code returned by the CSUTLDTC date-validation utility. A non-zero or error value here means the date entered by the operator (Origination or Processing Date) is invalid, causing the transaction to be rejected with an appropriate error message.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Reserved/unused space within the CSUTLDTC result structure. Has no direct business meaning; it is a padding field to align the result layout as required by the date-validation utility interface.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG-NUM
variables.description: A numeric message code returned by the CSUTLDTC utility identifying the specific type of date validation error encountered (e.g., invalid month, invalid day). Used to pinpoint exactly why a transaction date was rejected.

variables.name: CSUTLDTC-RESULT-MSG
variables.description: Human-readable error message returned by the CSUTLDTC utility when a transaction date fails validation. This message can be surfaced to the operator to explain why the Origination Date or Processing Date they entered was not accepted.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT02-INFO
variables.description: Group of fields carrying context information from the transaction list screen (COTRN00C) into this Add Transaction program — including pagination state and the transaction selected by the operator for reference or pre-population.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT02-TRNID-FIRST
variables.description: The Transaction ID of the first record displayed on the current page of the transaction list. Used to maintain correct pagination context when navigating between the transaction list and the add transaction screen.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT02-TRNID-LAST
variables.description: The Transaction ID of the last record displayed on the current page of the transaction list. Used alongside CDEMO-CT02-TRNID-FIRST to track the operator's position in the transaction ledger when returning from the add screen.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT02-PAGE-NUM
variables.description: The current page number within the transaction list that the operator was viewing before navigating to the Add Transaction screen. Allows the system to return the operator to the same page of the list after the add operation completes.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT02-NEXT-PAGE-FLG
variables.description: Flag indicating whether additional pages of transactions exist beyond the current page in the transaction list. Helps the list screen determine whether to offer a 'next page' navigation option to the operator.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating that more transaction records exist beyond the current page, so the operator can page forward in the transaction list.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the current page is the last page of the transaction list — no further records are available for forward navigation.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SEL-FLG
variables.description: Flag indicating whether the operator selected a specific transaction from the list screen before navigating to the Add Transaction screen. When set, the selected transaction's details may be used to pre-populate the form.

variables.name: CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED
variables.description: The Transaction ID of the specific transaction the operator selected from the transaction list screen (COTRN00C). Passed into this program so the selected transaction's data can be referenced or copied onto the add form to assist with repetitive data entry (PF5 function).

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS communication area passed between programs when control is transferred. Contains session state and context data (such as user identity, calling program, and navigation info) that persists across screen interactions, enabling the system to maintain a coherent operator session.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: Placeholder field representing the raw communication area data passed from the previous program. Its length (checked via EIBCALEN) tells the system whether a valid session exists — if zero, the operator is redirected to the sign-on screen, enforcing authenticated access before any transaction can be added.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration routine of the transaction-add program. It determines the operator's session state and key-press intent, then routes control to the appropriate business process — whether that is presenting a blank entry form, validating and saving a new transaction, navigating away, or clearing the screen.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph orchestrates the complete Enter-key workflow for adding a new transaction: it first validates all operator-entered data, then acts on the operator's explicit confirmation choice — committing the transaction only when 'Y' is entered, or re-prompting the operator when confirmation is absent or invalid.

paragraphs.name: VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph validates that the operator has supplied at least one valid account identifier — either an Account ID or a Card Number — and uses whichever was provided to automatically resolve and populate the other via the cross-reference file, ensuring both identifiers are present and verified before proceeding.

paragraphs.name: VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph enforces all mandatory field and format validation rules on the transaction data entered by the bank operator before any record is committed to the ledger. It ensures every required transaction attribute is present, correctly formatted, and calendar-valid, rejecting the entry and returning the operator to the data-entry screen with a targeted error message for each violation found.

paragraphs.name: ADD-TRANSACTION
paragraphs.description: This paragraph creates and permanently records a new credit card transaction in the master transaction ledger. It assigns the next available unique transaction ID, populates the full transaction record from the operator's screen input, and writes it to the ledger.

paragraphs.name: COPY-LAST-TRAN-DATA
paragraphs.description: This paragraph implements the PF5 'copy last transaction' feature, which retrieves the most recently recorded transaction from the ledger and pre-populates the data-entry screen with its details, helping operators efficiently enter repetitive or similar transactions without retyping all fields from scratch.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the operator's request to exit the transaction-add screen and return to the previous application screen. It ensures the session context is correctly handed back to the calling program, or defaults to the sign-on screen if no prior navigation origin is recorded.

paragraphs.name: SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Renders the transaction data-entry screen to the bank operator, displaying any validation error or status message, then suspends the program while preserving the current session state so the operator can review, correct, or confirm the transaction details before the next interaction.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-TRNADD-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Captures the data entered by the bank operator on the transaction addition screen, reading all typed field values into the program so they can be validated and processed. This is the point at which the operator's input — account details, transaction amounts, dates, and merchant information — is received from the terminal and made available for business rule checks.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: Populates the standard screen header area with application branding, the current date, and the current time before displaying the transaction entry form to the operator. This ensures every screen presented to the bank operator is consistently labelled and timestamped for audit and usability purposes.

paragraphs.name: READ-CXACAIX-FILE
paragraphs.description: Looks up the Card Number associated with a given Account ID by querying the alternate index on the card-to-account cross-reference file. If the account is not found or the lookup fails, the operator is immediately notified and the data-entry screen is re-displayed with an appropriate error message.

paragraphs.name: READ-CCXREF-FILE
paragraphs.description: Looks up the card-to-account cross-reference record using the Card Number supplied by the operator, confirming that the card exists in the system. Depending on the outcome, processing either continues normally or the screen is returned to the operator with an appropriate error message.

paragraphs.name: STARTBR-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph positions the transaction ledger at a specific transaction record, preparing the system to read backwards through recent transactions (e.g. to pre-fill the form via PF5). It handles cases where the transaction cannot be located or the ledger is temporarily unavailable.

paragraphs.name: READPREV-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the most recently preceding transaction record from the master transaction ledger, navigating backwards through the file by transaction ID. This supports the PF5 'copy last transaction' feature, allowing operators to pre-fill the data-entry form with details from the previous transaction to speed up repetitive data entry.

paragraphs.name: ENDBR-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: Closes the active sequential browse session against the transaction ledger, signalling that the program has finished scanning existing transaction records and is ready to proceed to the next processing step (such as writing a new transaction).

paragraphs.name: WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph attempts to permanently commit the validated and operator-confirmed transaction record to the master transaction ledger, then informs the operator of the outcome — success with the assigned Transaction ID, or a specific error requiring corrective action.

paragraphs.name: CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Resets the transaction data-entry screen to a completely blank state, discarding any previously entered or displayed data, and immediately re-presents the empty form to the operator ready for fresh input.

paragraphs.name: INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS
paragraphs.description: Resets the entire transaction data-entry screen to a clean, blank state so that a bank operator can begin entering a new credit card transaction from scratch. This ensures no residual data from a previous entry session can accidentally carry over into a new transaction record.
